Subject: Evaluating Redwood — commercial asks and transition credits

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked what we saw on latency and the dedup caching approach. Before we can move Redwood into procurement review, two commercial questions came up: 1) can you match CloudTron on unit costs for generator tokens (they're currently at $0.0009/token for our 8k sequences) and 2) do you have a standard "lift-and-shift" credit or implementation credit for migration work (we expect ~350M tokens/month and an S3 data export needed for model retraining).

Procurement also asked for a short checklist of technical parity items we need validated (KV cache behavior, quantized runtime performance, and any egress/ingress fees). Can you send a compact price-match proposal + the checklist so we can circulate internally?

Regards,

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood — commercial asks and transition credits

Emily — really appreciate the straightforward asks. I put together two practical options that balance economics and risk-transfer:

Option A — Parity Match + Onboard Credit (fast path)- Price match for generator tokens to $0.00085/token for the first 6 months (applies to usage up to 400M tokens/month)- $50k onboarding credit applied to professional services (migration, S3 ingestion, schema validation)- 60-day pilot SLA window with telemetry enabled for quality monitoring

Option B — Graduated Credits + Volume Commit (preferred for committed buyers)- $0.00095/token base, with a retroactive rebate to $0.00080/token if committed monthly volume >= 300M for 12 months- $80k onboarding credit + 10 days of dedicated SE time for integration and inference tuning- Assistance with export packaging for retraining (we'll accept an agreed subset of exported artifacts)

I attached a compact parity checklist (migration-checklist.csv) and a populated TCO worksheet for Atlas's numbers. High-level notes on technical parity:
- KV cache: compatible behavior with your prefix caching patterns; we will run a short workload validation during the pilot to confirm hit rates
- Quantized runtime: we support INT8 and FP16 profiles; profiler snapshot included in SOW-draft_v3.pdf
- Ingress/Egress: standard cloud egress fees apply for large S3 exports; we can absorb up to $5k of egress costs as part of Option A onboarding credit

Next step: if one of these aligns, can we get a procurement contact + timeline? Also, we'd like to propose a 4-week mutual action plan to scope migration and run a parity run.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Emily — quick technical clarifications from SE side to make sure the parity checklist is actionable:

1) Model runtime profile: can you confirm your typical sequence length distribution (p50/p90) and peak qps? That will determine kernel selection and batching targets.
2) KV cache footprint: do you rely on per-session long-term KV storage or ephemeral prefix caching? For large-scale sessions we recommend our continuous batching path with explicit cache TTLs.
3) Exports: Which artifacts are required for your retraining? We can provide tokens + prompt metadata exports and are willing to coordinate a secure S3 transfer.

If you can share a small sample (under NDA) we can run a 48-hour parity run against your 8k sequence profile and validate latency and per-token cost. Our goal is to produce a short parity report you can bring to procurement.

-Jordan will own the deployment playbook and monitoring hooks for the pilot.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
